prompt:
Samantha receives the following marks out of $100$ in seven of her eight courses:

| Course | Mark |
|---|---|
| Math | 94 |
| Science | 93 |
| English | 84 |
| Art | 81 |
| History | 74 |
| Phys Ed | 83 |
| Geography | 79 |

Determine her average mark in these seven courses.

solutions.title: Balance around 84
solutions.body:
Differences from $84$: $+10, +9, 0, -3, -10, -1, -5$. They add to $19 - 19 = 0$, so the average is $84$.

**Answer: 84**

prompt:
Samantha receives the following marks out of $100$ in seven of her eight courses:

| Course | Mark |
|---|---|
| Math | 94 |
| Science | 93 |
| English | 84 |
| Art | 81 |
| History | 74 |
| Phys Ed | 83 |
| Geography | 79 |

Before she finds out her actual French mark, Samantha calculates the highest possible average that she could obtain in all eight courses. Determine this average.

solutions.title: French mark of 100
solutions.body:
The best case is $100$ in French: $\frac{588 + 100}{8} = \frac{688}{8} = 86$.

**Answer: 86**

solutions.title: Share the extra
solutions.body:
A $100$ is $16$ above her current average of $84$; shared over $8$ courses it raises the average by $2$, to $86$.

**Answer: 86**

prompt:
Samantha receives the following marks out of $100$ in seven of her eight courses:

| Course | Mark |
|---|---|
| Math | 94 |
| Science | 93 |
| English | 84 |
| Art | 81 |
| History | 74 |
| Phys Ed | 83 |
| Geography | 79 |

When Samantha actually finds out her French mark, it turns out that her average in all eight courses is $85$. What is her actual French mark?

solutions.title: Use totals
solutions.body:
Eight courses averaging $85$ total $8 \times 85 = 680$. The first seven total $588$, so French is $680 - 588 = 92$.

**Answer: 92**

solutions.title: Halfway
solutions.body:
A French mark of $84$ keeps the average at $84$; a mark of $100$ gives $86$. The average changes evenly with the mark, so an average of $85$ (halfway) needs a mark halfway between $84$ and $100$: $92$.

**Answer: 92**

prompt:
Dmitri has a collection of identical cubes. Each cube is labelled with the integers $1$ to $6$ as shown in the following net: a row of four squares $4, 6, 3, 1$, with $5$ attached above the $6$ and $2$ attached below the $6$. (This net can be folded to make a cube, so $6$ is opposite $1$, $4$ is opposite $3$, and $5$ is opposite $2$.) He forms a pyramid by stacking layers of the cubes on a table, as shown, with the bottom layer being a $7$ by $7$ square of cubes (the layers are $7 \times 7$, $5 \times 5$, $3 \times 3$ and $1 \times 1$, each centred on the one below).

Determine the total number of cubes used to build the pyramid. Explain how you got your answer.

solutions.title: Layer by layer
solutions.body:
Layers: $7 \times 7 = 49$, $5 \times 5 = 25$, $3 \times 3 = 9$, and $1$. Total $49 + 25 + 9 + 1 = 84$.

**Answer: 84 cubes**

solutions.title: Odd squares
solutions.body:
The layers are the squares of the odd numbers $1, 3, 5, 7$: $1 + 9 + 25 + 49 = 84$.

**Answer: 84 cubes**

prompt:
Dmitri has a collection of identical cubes. Each cube is labelled with the integers $1$ to $6$ as shown in the following net: a row of four squares $4, 6, 3, 1$, with $5$ attached above the $6$ and $2$ attached below the $6$. (This net can be folded to make a cube, so $6$ is opposite $1$, $4$ is opposite $3$, and $5$ is opposite $2$.) He forms a pyramid by stacking layers of the cubes on a table, as shown, with the bottom layer being a $7$ by $7$ square of cubes (the layers are $7 \times 7$, $5 \times 5$, $3 \times 3$ and $1 \times 1$, each centred on the one below).

How many faces are visible after the pyramid is built and sitting on the table?

solutions.title: Look from above and from the sides
solutions.body:
From above you see a full $7 \times 7$ square of top faces (from all layers): $49$. From each of the four sides you see $1 + 3 + 5 + 7 = 16$ faces: $64$ in total. Bottom faces are hidden by the table. Total $49 + 64 = 113$.

**Answer: 113**

solutions.title: Cube by cube
solutions.body:
Top cube: $5$ faces. In each of the other layers, the $4$ corner cubes show $3$ faces each ($12$), and edge (non-corner) cubes show $2$: the $3 \times 3$ layer has $4$ of them ($8$ faces), the $5 \times 5$ layer $12$ ($24$), the $7 \times 7$ layer $20$ ($40$). Total $5 + (12 + 8) + (12 + 24) + (12 + 40) = 113$.

**Answer: 113**

prompt:
Dmitri has a collection of identical cubes. Each cube is labelled with the integers $1$ to $6$ as shown in the following net: a row of four squares $4, 6, 3, 1$, with $5$ attached above the $6$ and $2$ attached below the $6$. (This net can be folded to make a cube, so $6$ is opposite $1$, $4$ is opposite $3$, and $5$ is opposite $2$.) He forms a pyramid by stacking layers of the cubes on a table, as shown, with the bottom layer being a $7$ by $7$ square of cubes (the layers are $7 \times 7$, $5 \times 5$, $3 \times 3$ and $1 \times 1$, each centred on the one below).

Explain in detail how he should position the cubes so that if all of the visible numbers are added up, the total is as large as possible. What is this total?

solutions.title: Best faces for each kind of cube
solutions.body:
- **Top cube** (5 visible faces): hide the $1$; visible $2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 = 20$.
- **Corner cubes** (3 visible faces: top and two sides; $12$ of them): show $4, 5, 6$, which meet at a corner since no two of them are opposite. Each gives $15$: total $180$.
- **Edge cubes** (2 visible faces: top and one side; $4 + 12 + 20 = 36$ of them): show $5$ and $6$, which share an edge. Each gives $11$: total $396$.
- Hidden cubes contribute nothing.

Maximum total: $20 + 180 + 396 = 596$.

**Answer: 596**

solutions.title: Top view plus side views
solutions.body:
Put a $6$ on top of every cube: the $49$ top faces give $294$. The top cube also shows $2, 3, 4, 5$ on its sides: $14$. The other side faces ($4(3 + 5 + 7) = 60$) would ideally all be $5$, giving $300$, but each of the $12$ corner cubes shows two side faces and has only one $5$, so one of those becomes a $4$ ($4, 5, 6$ meet at a vertex): subtract $12$.

Total: $294 + 14 + 300 - 12 = 596$.

**Answer: 596**

prompt:
Three congruent isosceles triangles $DAO$, $AOB$ and $OBC$ have $AD = AO = OB = BC = 10$ and $AB = DO = OC = 12$. These triangles are arranged to form trapezoid $ABCD$, as shown. Point $P$ is on side $AB$ so that $OP$ is perpendicular to $AB$.

What is the length of $OP$? Explain how you got your answer.

solutions.title: Pythagoras
solutions.body:
In isosceles $\triangle AOB$ ($AO = OB$), the perpendicular from $O$ bisects $AB$, so $AP = 6$. Then $OP = \sqrt{10^2 - 6^2} = \sqrt{64} = 8$.

**Answer: 8**

solutions.title: 3-4-5 triangle
solutions.body:
$\triangle AOP$ has hypotenuse $10$ and leg $6$: it is a $6$–$8$–$10$ triangle (twice $3$–$4$–$5$), so $OP = 8$.

**Answer: 8**

prompt:
Three congruent isosceles triangles $DAO$, $AOB$ and $OBC$ have $AD = AO = OB = BC = 10$ and $AB = DO = OC = 12$. These triangles are arranged to form trapezoid $ABCD$, as shown. Point $P$ is on side $AB$ so that $OP$ is perpendicular to $AB$.

What is the area of trapezoid $ABCD$? Explain how you got your answer.

solutions.title: Three congruent triangles
solutions.body:
Each triangle has base $12$ and height $8$, area $\frac12 \cdot 12 \cdot 8 = 48$. Three of them: $144$.

**Answer: 144**

solutions.title: Trapezoid formula
solutions.body:
Parallel sides $AB = 12$ and $DC = DO + OC = 24$, height $OP = 8$: area $\frac12 (12 + 24)(8) = 144$.

**Answer: 144**

prompt:
Three congruent isosceles triangles $DAO$, $AOB$ and $OBC$ have $AD = AO = OB = BC = 10$ and $AB = DO = OC = 12$. These triangles are arranged to form trapezoid $ABCD$, as shown. Point $P$ is on side $AB$ so that $OP$ is perpendicular to $AB$.

Point $X$ is the midpoint of $AD$ and point $Y$ is the midpoint of $BC$. When $X$ and $Y$ are joined, the trapezoid is divided into two smaller trapezoids. What is the ratio of the area of trapezoid $ABYX$ to the area of trapezoid $XYCD$? Explain how you got your answer.

solutions.title: Find XY
solutions.body:
$XY$ joins the midpoints of the legs, so it is parallel to the bases, halfway up: each small trapezoid has height $4$. The midline of a trapezoid is the average of the bases: $XY = \frac{12 + 24}{2} = 18$.

- $ABYX$: $\frac12(12 + 18)(4) = 60$.
- $XYCD$: $\frac12(18 + 24)(4) = 84$.

Ratio $60 : 84 = 5 : 7$.

**Answer: $5 : 7$**

solutions.title: Twelve small triangles
solutions.body:
Join the midpoints of all the sides of the three big triangles. Each big triangle splits into $4$ congruent small triangles (sides $5, 5, 6$), so the trapezoid is made of $12$ equal small triangles. The line $XY$ passes through these midpoints; above it lie $5$ small triangles and below it $7$. So the ratio of areas is $5 : 7$.

**Answer: $5 : 7$**

prompt: How many of the positive integers from $1$ to $100$, inclusive, do not contain the digit $7$? Explain how you got your answer.

solutions.title: Count those with a 7
solutions.body:
Ending in $7$: $7, 17, \dots, 97$ ($10$ numbers). Tens digit $7$: $70, \dots, 79$ ($10$). $77$ is in both, so $19$ numbers contain a $7$. Answer: $100 - 19 = 81$.

**Answer: 81**

solutions.title: Two-digit strings
solutions.body:
Replace $100$ by $0$ (neither has a $7$) and write $0$–$99$ as $00$–$99$. Each digit has $9$ choices other than $7$: $9 \times 9 = 81$.

**Answer: 81**

prompt: How many of the positive integers from $1$ to $2000$, inclusive, do not contain the digit $7$? Explain how you got your answer.

solutions.title: Four-digit strings
solutions.body:
Replace $2000$ by $0000$ (neither contains $7$) and count $0000$–$1999$: the first digit is $0$ or $1$ ($2$ choices), and each of the other three digits has $9$ choices. Total $2 \times 9^3 = 1458$.

**Answer: 1458**

solutions.title: Blocks of 100
solutions.body:
Each block of $100$ ($1$–$100$, $101$–$200$, ...) whose hundreds digit isn't $7$ and doesn't end at a number like $700$ contains $81$ such numbers. Blocks $601$–$700$ and $1601$–$1700$ have $80$ (since $700$, $1700$ contain $7$); blocks $701$–$800$ and $1701$–$1800$ have only $1$ ($800$, $1800$). The other $16$ blocks have $81$. Total $16 \cdot 81 + 2 \cdot 80 + 2 \cdot 1 = 1458$.

**Answer: 1458**

prompt: Determine the sum of all of the positive integers from $1$ to $2006$, inclusive, that do not contain the digit $7$. Explain how you got your answer.

solutions.title: Blocks of 100
solutions.body:
From $1$ to $100$ the numbers containing a $7$ are $7, 17, \dots, 67, 70, \dots, 79, 87, 97$, with sum $1188$, so the good numbers sum to $5050 - 1188 = 3862$ ($81$ numbers).

A block $100k + 1$ to $100k + 100$ (hundreds digit not $7$) has the same $81$ numbers shifted by $100k$: sum $3862 + 8100k$. Adjust where $7$ appears: blocks ending in $700$ or $1700$ lose that number, and the blocks $701$–$800$, $1701$–$1800$ contain only $800$, $1800$. Summing the $18$ full blocks for $k \in \{0,\dots,6, 8,\dots,16, 18, 19\}$, the corrections, and $2001$–$2006$:
$$18(3862) + 8100(166) - 700 - 1700 + 800 + 1800 + 12\,021 = 1\,426\,337.$$

**Answer: 1 426 337**
